name: Biao
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Liang, Jingui. 2024 [title page dated March 2025]. A Grammar of Biao, Southeast China. PhD thesis, Asia Institute, University of Melbourne. 479 pp. Open Access, Minerva Access,https://hdl.handle.net/11343/355886(Glottolog ref 714767).
catalog_locator: Ch. 2 Phonology: sec. 2.3.1 Monophthongs, p.50 (stress denial); sec. 2.4 Medials p.53 (syllable-internal 'stress of a final'); sec. 2.6 Tones pp.55-57 (tone inventory, tone sandhi). Ch. 3 Morphology: sec. 3.4 Affixation p.76 ('stress on the root morphemes'); sec. 3.4.1.3 p.81 (a55 unstressed); sec. 3.4.1.5 p.83 (to214/lak12/a55 sesquisyllabic).
catalog_quote: There is no feature such as tenseness, nasal or stress in Biao. [p.50] ... Biao has a system of 6 tones in smooth syllables, i.e. syllables ending in vowels or nasal consonants -m, -n, -ŋ, including high level 55, dipping 214, high fall 53, low rise-fall 132, rise 35 and low level 22. There are 4 tones in checked syllables, namely syllables ending in -p, -t, -k, of which 3 tones are shared with the smooth syllables. [p.55] ... Tone sandhi can be found in Biao. When syllables which combine with high pitch tones such as Tone 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 precede other syllables, the high pitch tones change to mid level pitch 33. When syllables which combine with low pitch tones, including Tone 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10, precede other syllables, these low pitch tones become mid-low fall pitch 21. [p.57] ... Biao, like many Kra-Dai languages, lacks genuine affixes, but there are a significant number of affixable morphemes which can be analysed as affixes. In this case, affixable morphemes are slight sounds, with the stress on the root morphemes. [p.76] ... a55 is unstressed. Accordingly, these examples would prosodically have an unstressed syllable a55. [p.81] ... to214 is unstressed here, that is, prosodically, it takes half of the metrical foot, forming what Matisoff (2003) says about SE Asia and Tibeto-Burman sesquisyllable. This is also the case with lak12 and a55. [p.83]
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (479 pp, text; the PDF's metadata gives the title 'A Grammar of Biao, Southeast China', Jingui Liang, Asia Institute, University of Melbourne, PhD thesis, title page dated March 2025, Glottolog ref 714767 lists it as 2024) plus its text dump. All three quoted passages are present verbatim at the stated locators: (1) printed p.50 = p.66 (extracted text confirms both the sentence and the page number '50'), end of sec. 2.3 monophthongs: 'There is no feature such as tenseness, nasal or stress in Biao.'; (2) p.75 sec. 3.4 Affixation: 'Biao, like many Kra-Dai languages, lacks genuine affixes, but there are a significant number of affixable morphemes which can be analysed as affixes.…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Biao (Shidong) is a tone language with 10 tones (6 on smooth, 4 on checked syllables); the author states there is no stress feature in the phonology. The only prominence asymmetry described is morphological/prosodic: a handful of prefixes (a55, to214, lak12) and other affix-like morphemes are 'slight'/unstressed with prominence on the root, giving sesquisyllable-like words; and tone sandhi reduces non-final syllables (high tones -> 33, low tones -> 21) while the final syllable keeps its citation tone.
new_statements.exceptions: Unstressed prefixes a55 (kinship), to214 (animals), lak12 and 'affixable morphemes' generally carry less prominence than roots (pp.75, 82-83). 'Stress of a final' after medial i (p.53) refers to the syllable nucleus, not word stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the segmental/suprasegmental feature inventory of the (monosyllable-based) phonology; prefix/root prominence is discussed at the word level in the morphology chapter; tone sandhi (p.57) applies to any non-final syllable preceding another syllable (domain not delimited further). Data are elicited citation forms and texts from Shidong Township speakers.
new_statements.identity_note: Liang 2024's fieldwork site is Shuanglong Village, Shidong Township, Huaiji County (main consultant Xu Wenhai, b.1964), i.e. exactly Shidong Biao [biao1253]; the author treats Yonggu and Dagang as 'vernacular areas' of one language, whereas Glottolog splits Biaoic into Shidong Biao [biao1253], Yonggu Biao [yong1283] and Dagang-Baoshan-Liangcun [daga1277]. Lin 2009 (also saved) describes Yonggu Biao [yong1283]; Yang 2022 describes Chang'an (Fengkai), a northern variety closest to daga1277.

tone_statements.citation: Solnit, David B. 2007. Review of "A study of the Biao language 标话研究" [Biaohua yanjiu], by Liang Min and Zhang Junru (Beijing: Central University for Nationalities Press, 2002). Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 30(2): 215-229.
tone_statements.quote: There are six tones in unchecked syllables and four in checked syllables. Tones are notated in the way that is standard for Chinese descriptions of Kadai languages, with numerals 1-10, even numbers for tones conditioned by previously voiced initials (sometimes called the low series) and odd numbers conditioned by all other initial types (the high series). [...] The ‘high’ series 1 3 5 7 9 is in fact relatively higher in pitch than the ‘low’ series 2 4 6 8 10. Similarly the high-series tones merge to mid-level in sandhi with a following syllable, while the low-series tones merge to low-level in this environment.
tone_statements.summary: 10 tone categories (6 on smooth syllables, 4 on checked) from a plain two-way voicing split; pitch-only (no phonation); non-final sandhi neutralises high series to mid level and low series to low level; review of Liang & Zhang 2002 (Shidong reference dialect).

sources.note: Describes YONGGU Biao (Glottolog yong1283), not Shidong. Sec.2.1.3: 6 smooth + 4 checked tones; sec.2.2 point 5: '永固标话有简单的连读变调：以前字变调为主，结尾的音节一般不变.. 高平调的音节一般变为中平调[33]，其他音节一般变为低降调[21]' (simple tone sandhi: the preceding syllable changes, the final syllable generally does not). No statement using 重音/轻声/轻读; silent on word stress as such.

sources.note: Biao has six tones in unchecked and four in checked syllables, numbered 1-10 in the Kadai convention (odd = high series from proto-voiceless initials, even = low series from proto-voiced); tones 1/2 < proto-tone A, 3/4 < the proto-tone matching Chinese shang (Li's C), 5/6 < qu (Li's B), 7-10 checked; tones described purely by pitch, no non-modal phonation (noted as unusual for Kadai); simple two-way voicing-conditioned split with no aspiration/glottalization conditioning; in sandhi before a following syllable all high-series tones merge to mid level and all low-series tones to low level.
